titleEn: Shoes in Their Place, Just Like That!

pages.text: "I'm home!" Pongi came back from playing on the tied-up boat. She tossed her boots, her vest, and her basket into the doorway. The oar rolled away. Throwing things was fun, but picking them up wasn't fun at all.
"Ouch!" Pongi stepped on the oar and landed on her bottom with a thump. Boots and a vest lay under her feet. There was nowhere to step in the doorway.
But she couldn't see her basket. "Where did my basket go?" Pongi looked all around. She lifted the vest and looked under the sofa, but it wasn't there. Her shoulders drooped.
Mom, wearing her headscarf, came to the doorway carrying Pongi's brother and his shell. She looked around and smiled. "Pongi, I'll show you a little doorway magic."

Mom pointed to the shoe spaces. There were three in a row. Boots stood neatly in Dad's space and Mom's space, but Pongi's was empty. "When a space is empty, things end up lying on the floor. They get stepped on or hidden."

"But when you tidy up..." Mom picked up Pongi's boots and stood them in her space. "In their place, they won't get stepped on, and missing things turn up again. Shoes in their place, just like that!" Pongi's paws were already moving.
Pongi put her vest on the shelf and stood the oar beside the door. Mom sang, "Shoes in their place, just like that!" Her brother waved his shell. "Like that!"
When Pongi moved the oar, the basket appeared in the corner by the door! "My basket!" She hugged it and thumped her tail. "When I tidy up, hidden things come back!"

That evening, Pongi came back from the boat and put things down one by one. "One, boots in their place! Two, vest on the shelf! Three, oar beside the door!" Before Mom said a word, the doorway was already tidy.
Mom gave Pongi a snug hug. "You're the doorway captain, Pongi!" Tidy up after playing, and the things you want turn up too. "Shoes in their place, just like that! Tomorrow too!" Pongi smiled.
